question: Does a crate_universe hub expose BUILD.<name>-<version>.bazel under Bzlmod; does override_repo of a spoke leave the digest untouched; what happens to a stale override after a bump?
verdict: hub file: REFUTED; cargo-bazel-lock.json untouched by override_repo: CONFIRMED; MODULE.bazel.lock untouched: only because the crate extension is reproducible in this fixture and has no entry in the lock (see module_lock_note), not shown for a recorded hub; stale override: hard error (see cells[].stale_override_after_bump)

environment.launcher: at capture time the campaign launcher exported TEST_TMPDIR on every command, which puts the Bazel server in test mode (TestType.isInTest)
environment.why: Bazel's own switches for production behaviour in test mode. Without them a failing module extension during `build` on 7.7.2 is `FATAL: bazel crashed due to an internal error`, exit 37, instead of the ordinary error with exit 1
environment.steps: Q4a-bump-build-no-repin is cells[].stale_override_after_bump.build_without_repin; Q4c-bump-build is cells[].stale_override_after_bump.build. Every other step of every cell has the same exit code in both runs

module_lock_note: Every module_lock_unchanged: true below is about a lock with no entry for the crate extension (cells[].crate_extension_in_module_lock is false, cells[].module_lock names the absent key). For an extension that has an entry, Bazel hashes the repo overrides into usagesDigest: adding override_repo changes that one line and --lockfile_mode=error then fails until the lock is refreshed (campaign probes, toy extensions: rc-ignore-substitution S10 on 7.7.2, lock diff one usagesDigest line; starlark-include lock-touch table on 7.7.2, 8.8.2, 9.3.2 and 10.0.0rc3, `mod deps --lockfile_mode=error` exit 2; source: bazel@8.8.2 SingleExtensionUsagesValue.trimForEvaluation keeps getRepoOverrides()). A hub without `lockfile` or `cargo_lockfile` is not reproducible and has an entry; that case was not run here
fixture: rust_binary //:app on cfg-if =1.0.0; crate.from_cargo(name = 'crates', cargo_lockfile, manifests, lockfile = '//:cargo-bazel-lock.json'); //:oracle builds only against the patched crate (it calls cfg_if::socket_patched())

source_reading.claim: at every Bzlmod tag read the extension passes each spoke its BUILD text as build_file_content and puts only BUILD.bazel and defs.bzl (later also alias_rules.bzl, crates.bzl and per-alias packages) into the hub

cells.crate_extension_in_module_lock_reason: reproducible: rules_rust 0.75.0 returns extension_metadata(reproducible = True) when every hub tag sets both `lockfile` and `cargo_lockfile` (crate_universe/extensions.bzl:990, 1176-1186, 1223-1224), as this fixture's one tag does, so Bazel writes no entry for it
